summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,665.93, down 0.15%, a nearly flat day as investors held their breath before Nvidia reported earnings after the bell. The economy grew at a 1.5% annual pace in the second quarter, confirmed by a second government estimate, and the Fed's preferred inflation measure, called core PCE, rose 0.2% in July and 3.3% over the past year according to press coverage, keeping interest rate cuts off the table for now. Bitcoin slipped to 78,048 while gold held near flat at 4,644. Tomorrow brings Canadian bank earnings from CM.TO and RY.TO plus weekly unemployment claims, and Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday.
